issue_context.title: udev_event_apply_format (often silently) truncates its output without returning an error
issue_context.body:
udev_event_apply_format does not let the caller determine if an error or other truncation has occurred: Unlike the strpcpy family of functions, it always returns a positive value (assuming the [assert](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v249/src/udev/udev-event.c#L489) is correct). In most cases, it also does not log a warning.

This is especially problematic for rules that use [`PROGRAM="..."`](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v249/src/udev/udev-rules.c#L1696)/[`RUN="..."`](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v249/src/udev/udev-rules.c#L2202-L2205)/etc where the command is silently truncated if it exceeds 1023 characters (UDEV_PATH_SIZE-1), which causes the wrong command to be executed; the silent truncation makes this particularly hard to debug (e.g. https://github.com/raspberrypi/linux/issues/3779#issuecomment-758029604).

Curiously, the return value of `udev_event_apply_format` appears to be ignored everywhere it is called (it's cast to `void`).

There are four main cases of truncation:
* The two error cases (["Invalid format string"](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v249/src/udev/udev-event.c#L461), ["Failed to substitute variable ... or apply format"](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v249/src/udev/udev-event.c#L473-L475)) break out of the loop (and ignore the rest of the format string). As these are already special-cased, returning an error here would be easy.
* When the [character-by-character copy](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v249/src/udev/udev-event.c#L464-L465) runs out of space, it also simply breaks out of the loop. Again, since this is already special-cased, it could easily return an error.
* [udev_event_subst_format](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v249/src/udev/udev-event.c#L234) ignores the return value from any of its calls to `strpcpy(&s, l, ...)` or similar (which return 0 to indicate truncation). It looks like this could be changed to take `char **dest` and simply return the result of strpcpy in most cases (which would allow truncation to be detected), with minor modifications to the handling of [FORMAT_SUBST_LINKS](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v249/src/udev/udev-event.c#L406-L413) (which calls strpcpy/strpcpyl multiple times) and [replace_whitespace](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v249/src/udev/udev-event.c#L480-L483).

`udev_event_subst_format` also substitutes many error cases (mainly `-ENOENT`) with the empty string (`goto null_terminate;`). While this might be reasonable if the format string is a single substitution, this is less likely to be the desired behaviour otherwise. For example, `$devnode`/`%N` is substituted with the empty string on ENOENT, which doesn't make sense in its typical uses cases, e.g. Debian udev 232-25+deb9u13 seems to use it entirely within command lines:
```
> grep -rE '\$devnode|%N' /lib/udev /etc/udev/
Binary file /lib/udev/hwdb.bin matches
/lib/udev/rules.d/75-probe_mtd.rules:KERNEL=="mtd*ro", IMPORT{program}="mtd_probe $devnode"
/lib/udev/rules.d/64-btrfs.rules:IMPORT{builtin}="btrfs ready $devnode"
/lib/udev/rules.d/60-persistent-storage.rules:KERNEL=="sd*[!0-9]|sr*", ENV{ID_SERIAL}!="?*", SUBSYSTEMS=="scsi", ATTRS{vendor}=="ATA", IMPORT{program}="ata_id --export $devnode"
/lib/udev/rules.d/60-persistent-storage.rules:KERNEL=="sd*[!0-9]|sr*", ENV{ID_SERIAL}!="?*", SUBSYSTEMS=="scsi", ATTRS{type}=="5", ATTRS{scsi_level}=="[6-9]*", IMPORT{program}="ata_id --export $devnode"
/lib/udev/rules.d/60-persistent-storage.rules:KERNEL=="sd*[!0-9]|sr*", ENV{ID_SERIAL}!="?*", ATTR{removable}=="0", SUBSYSTEMS=="usb", IMPORT{program}="ata_id --export $devnode"
/lib/udev/rules.d/60-persistent-storage.rules:KERNEL=="sd*[!0-9]|sr*", ENV{ID_SERIAL}!="?*", IMPORT{program}="scsi_id --export --whitelisted -d $devnode", ENV{ID_BUS}="scsi"
/lib/udev/rules.d/60-persistent-storage.rules:KERNEL=="cciss*", ENV{DEVTYPE}=="disk", ENV{ID_SERIAL}!="?*", IMPORT{program}="scsi_id --export --whitelisted -d $devnode", ENV{ID_BUS}="cciss"
/lib/udev/rules.d/60-persistent-v4l.rules:IMPORT{program}="v4l_id $devnode"
/lib/udev/rules.d/60-persistent-storage-tape.rules:SUBSYSTEM=="scsi_generic", SUBSYSTEMS=="scsi", ATTRS{type}=="8", IMPORT{program}="scsi_id --sg-version=3 --export --whitelisted -d $devnode", \
/lib/udev/rules.d/60-cdrom_id.rules:ENV{DISK_EJECT_REQUEST}=="?*", RUN+="cdrom_id --eject-media $devnode", GOTO="cdrom_end"
/lib/udev/rules.d/60-cdrom_id.rules:IMPORT{program}="cdrom_id --lock-media $devnode"
```

There's also potential truncation in the handling of FORMAT_SUBST_ATTR (within [udev_resolve_subsys_kernel](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/af55491028a0722088a16ff6e20de2d6f1507640/src/shared/udev-util.c#L550-L559), and in the [strscpy of the value from device_get_sysattr_value_maybe_from_netlink or device_get_sysattr_value_maybe_from_netlink](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/src/udev/udev-event.c#L366)), but it is perhaps reasonable to assume that the length of these attributes do not exceed UDEV_NAME_SIZE.

review_comments: Please add some tests for all the new functions. Those things are usually tricky to get right in all corner cases.
this could also return EINVAL, no? Shouldn't it check explicitly for ENOMEM before returning?
